name: TOI-1873
title: TOI-1873: two planets and a candidate, TESS + NEID
notes: Real data. TESS (13 sectors, detrended by EXOTIC, 10-minute bins around every transit) and 37 NEID velocities. b and c are confirmed; d is a candidate with three transits, put at its shortest allowed period (128.598 d). Radius, inclination, period, mid-time and mass of each planet, the limb darkening and the NEID jitter are free; a/R★ follows from Kepler’s law, orbits are circular. Compare with the published two-planet pyaneti fit in the Methods page’s Reproducibility table.

warnings: Not converged: the budget of 1,500,000 likelihood calls was used up with 2.6% of the evidence possibly still inside the live points. The posterior is a weighted sample of what was explored (4603 effective samples) and may still narrow or move; ln Z is what was found so far, in practice a lower limit, not to be used for comparing models.
The posterior of N alias (d) runs into the upper edge of its prior. That is fine if the edge is physical (i = 90°, zero jitter or mass: read the result as a limit); otherwise widen the prior.
The posterior of Mp (d) runs into the lower edge of its prior. That is fine if the edge is physical (i = 90°, zero jitter or mass: read the result as a limit); otherwise widen the prior.
The posterior of LD 1 runs into the upper edge of its prior. That is fine if the edge is physical (i = 90°, zero jitter or mass: read the result as a limit); otherwise widen the prior.
The posterior of LD 2 runs into the lower edge of its prior. That is fine if the edge is physical (i = 90°, zero jitter or mass: read the result as a limit); otherwise widen the prior.

The posterior has 3 separate peaks in i (d): 89.6508 (89%), 89.8032 (7.1%), 89.755 (3.7%). Means and error bars over all of them describe none of them: narrow the prior to one peak, or report them separately. Their relative weights are uncertain, because most points came from slice sampling, which does not move between peaks.
i (d) and N alias (d) are -0.96 correlated: the data constrain a combination of the two. Fix one, give one a tighter prior, or fit the combination.
